dimensions.name: Contract & semantics reverse-engineering

evidence.note: Before writing server code, read helpers.py (incl. tail), conftest, run.sh, README, every test file, and all oracle_fixtures JSON — systematically extracting the concrete request/response shapes the first-party client exercises.
Deliberate library choice (fastapi/uvicorn/openpyxl/websockets) after checking installed deps, rather than defaulting blindly.
Grounded tricky formula semantics in Excel: bare TRUE/FALSE idents, changed-cells return semantics (re-checked against test_deps), and LAMBDA-via-LET apply resolution.

Verified openpyxl's actual conditional-formatting API by loading its own export and correcting range=sqref and color=fgColor — confirming the library truly supports the required round-trip rather than assuming.
Probed Excel-specific behaviors (0.1+0.2 shown at 15 sig digits, iterative fixed-point Gauss-Seidel convergence, spill ghost blocking) to align with the LibreOffice oracle.
Re-consulted the client/tests when new subsystems were reached (grep changed_cells_returned, grep COUNT) rather than only at the start.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent systematically read helpers.py, run.sh, and the entire smoke suite plus oracle fixtures up front to map the wire contract, chose libraries deliberately, and repeatedly grounded genuinely tricky behavior (spill ghosts, iterative fixed-point, Excel display rounding, openpyxl CF API) in Excel/LibreOffice semantics while verifying library support — squarely anchor 8. It stops short of 10 because there is no durable cross-referenced contract artifact and much of the deeper semantic grounding was reactive to test failures rather than proactively surfaced and reconciled against the oracle.

dimensions.name: Sequencing the feature surface into checkable milestones

evidence.note: Stated a coarse plan ('build core skeleton first, then iterate') and named a dependency-respecting file structure (refs→parser→functions→engine→server→store→xlsx→html), but this is construction ordering, not a milestone hierarchy with per-item done-checks.

Built the entire feature surface — engine, ~150 functions, all routes, persistence, xlsx, SPA — in one monolithic push before running any test. High-risk load-bearing layers (graph, spill, recompute) were not isolated or verified first; the opposite of front-loading risk.

First and only checkpoint arrives after everything is built: import, start server, run the smoke suite. The dev smoke suite becomes the de-facto done-check, applied to the whole product at once rather than per-milestone.

Post-build 'hardening' phase driven by ad-hoc concern lists (persistence, performance probes for 1k chain / 100k import / 5k fan-out). These are targeted checks but reactive, not part of a pre-planned dependency-ordered milestone sequence.
Late phase is repeated re-running of the smoke suite (131/131) plus edge-case probes; no re-ordering or living milestone plan — a static 'build-all-then-verify' pattern throughout.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent showed coarse phasing (explore → monolithic build → smoke-suite checkpoint → fix → harden) and used run.sh as a recurring runnable done-check, placing it above a flat unordered to-do list (anchor 3). But it built the entire interdependent surface before any verification, never front-loading a minimal live-server/persistence/core-round-trip green before breadth, and defined no explicit per-milestone done-criteria sequenced by dependency and risk (anchors 8-10). It only partially meets anchor 5's 'skeleton-first with per-stage checkpoints,' so it lands at 4.

dimensions.name: Self-built verification beyond the smoke suite

evidence.note: Built its own performance probes directly targeting the spec's stated ceilings: 1000-cell linear chain, 100k sparse import, 5000-cell fan-out propagation — benchmarking beyond anything in the smoke suite.
Constructed an ad-hoc test that surfaced a BIN2DEC/DEC2HEX tokenizer bug (CELL regex swallowing 'BIN2'), diagnosed it, and fixed it — a self-built check driving a fix.
Exercised xlsx round-trip via openpyxl, found conditional-formatting import bugs (range object stringified, wrong fgColor), fixed CF import and re-verified round-trip.
Hand-checked currency/percent format output against expected Excel rendering ($9,999.50), found the $ placement bug, fixed the template filler.

Spot-checked lookups, date functions, and COUNT against expected Excel values via python one-liners; correctly recognized a COUNT 'failure' as stale-workbook false alarm rather than trusting it blindly.
Ran dev_tests/run.sh repeatedly throughout, using the 131-test green run as a regression baseline after each fix — but treated it as a floor, not the finish line.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent went well beyond running run.sh: it wrote targeted probes for the stated performance bounds, exercised xlsx/CF round-trips through openpyxl, hand-checked many individual functions (BIN2DEC, lookups, dates, COUNT, currency/percent formatting) against expected Excel behavior, and consistently used those checks' failures to drive fixes — squarely matching the level-8 anchor. It stops short of level 10 because expected values were mostly grounded in the agent's own recall of Excel semantics rather than a systematic Excel/LibreOffice oracle harness, and much of the 'verification' late in the run is prose reasoning about edge cases rather than executed tests.

dimensions.name: Tracking done-vs-remaining across a huge surface

evidence.note: First test run anchors progress quantitatively ('120 passing, 11 failing') and enumerates the specific failing areas to address — tracking done-vs-remaining against the smoke suite rather than by feel.

Post-green, produces enumerated concern lists across feature families (persistence, perf, formula corpus, XLSX artifacts) and marks function status ('SUMPRODUCT ✓ (added)', 'SUBTOTAL? Not yet', 'DATEDIF? Not yet') — an informal function-catalog ledger.
Repeatedly reruns the 131-test suite after each fix, reconciling live state against verification results and watching for regressions rather than trusting self-report.
Detects a false alarm — recognizes COUNT=3 was stale-workbook contamination, not a real bug, and explicitly avoids chasing it, showing it can distinguish real vs phantom issues instead of looping.
Isolates BIN2DEC tokenizer bug, fixes, restarts, verifies, moves on — no circular re-debugging.

Tracking is entirely prose-based; never adopts a persistent ledger (TodoWrite available but unused), so coverage of the ~150 functions is re-derived by mental scanning rather than maintained granularly.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently anchors progress against the smoke-test count, enumerates function-level status with ✓/not-yet markers, reruns tests after each fix, and catches a stale-state false alarm without looping — clearly above the simple 'checklist of major features' anchor (5). But it never maintains a truly live granular ledger of the full catalog/endpoint families; whole categories are surfaced opportunistically via mental scanning ('let me think about what else could be missing'), falling short of the sustained, systematic done/partial/not-started tracking described at anchor 8. This places it at 6.

dimensions.name: Course-correcting on falsified Excel/perf assumptions

evidence.note: Diagnosed that recompute()'s changed set omitted literal dirty cells (only AST cells were added) — a correction to the dependency/recompute model, not a local patch.
Recognized LAMBDA-via-LET failed because `triple(7)` parsed as a function call; reworked call-eval to resolve apply when the name isn't a builtin — an assumption-level design change.
Traced AND()=#NAME? to bare TRUE/FALSE being parsed as identifiers; revised name evaluation rather than special-casing the test.
Root-caused stale BIN2DEC to the CELL token regex matching `BIN2` ahead of IDENT — fixed tokenizer precedence.
Correctly attributed a COUNT=3 anomaly to leftover workbook state (test contamination) instead of the engine, avoiding a spurious fix — diagnosing root vs surface.
Fixed CF round-trip by correcting openpyxl API assumptions (sqref, fgColor vs bgColor).
Consistently restarts the server and reruns the full suite after each fix, re-verifying corrections.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent repeatedly recognizes when a failure signals a wrong underlying assumption — the recompute changed-set model (58), parse-time vs eval-time apply resolution (59), token precedence (88), name evaluation (55-56) — and reworks the relevant design rather than piling on band-aids, re-verifying each time. Its refusal to 'fix' the COUNT false alarm (116/472) shows root-cause discipline. It stops short of 10 because corrections are largely reactive to the smoke suite rather than proactively detected, and some divergences (batched spill validation) were deferred rather than reworked, placing it solidly at the anchor-8 level.

dimensions.name: Coverage allocation under finite effort

evidence.note: Built the full function catalog breadth-first across all families (math, stats, distributions, financial, date, engineering, database, lookup, text, dynamic-array) before any depth work, securing broad working coverage of common functions rather than perfecting one area.

After smoke tests pass, explicitly enumerates and prioritizes hidden-grading concerns (persistence, performance, the 200-formula hidden corpus, XLSX round-trip) — reasoning about graded return, not arbitrary ordering.

Explicitly reasons 'the hidden formula corpus is 200 cases. Let me check categories I might have missed' and audits for gaps (SUMPRODUCT ✓, SUBTOTAL?, DATEDIF?, SUMSQ) — targeting broad catalog coverage where marginal formulas add score.

Consciously defers a complex low-yield edge case (batched spill-ghost validation within a single request): 'Let me defer this for now since it's complex... the test only uses separate calls' — deliberate timeboxing of a niche.

Sustained post-smoke phase revisits many subsystems (CF round-trip, sort typing, format-only patches, iterative calc, goal seek) to shore up broad correctness across endpoint families rather than over-polishing one, showing revisited but reactive allocation.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent secured broad working coverage of the entire function catalog and endpoint surface before deep edge-case work, then explicitly reasoned about graded return against the hidden ~200-formula corpus (steps 68, 76) and consciously deferred a low-yield complex edge case (step 103) — squarely matching the level-8 anchor. It falls short of 10 because the allocation, while revisited after verification, is largely reactive gap-hunting rather than a deliberately timeboxed, marginal-yield-driven reallocation strategy.

rubric.task_read: This is an extremely long-horizon, high-complexity build: a full Excel-clone product (persistent HTTP server + SPA + WebSocket collab) with a formula engine spanning ~150 functions, Excel-365 dynamic arrays/spill, a dependency graph with performance-bounded dirty recompute, xlsx/CSV round-trip, and a large analyst surface (defined names, formats, conditional formatting, pivots, locale, validation, goal seek, iterative calc). The exact wire contract is under-specified and must be reverse-engineered from an existing Python client, and grading is on a much larger HIDDEN suite plus value-by-value comparison against a LibreOffice oracle. This task demands maximal, sustained meta-work across all five faculties: deep upfront orientation on the contract, aggressive decomposition/sequencing of an enormous surface, self-built verification well beyond the smoke suite, tight progress tracking, and constant course-correction as Excel edge cases falsify assumptions.

dimensions.name: Contract & semantics reverse-engineering
dimensions.description: Extracting the exact wire shapes from /dev_tests/helpers.py and the smoke suite, and grounding formula/feature behavior in Excel/LibreOffice semantics, before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The wire shapes are defined ONLY by what the first-party client calls, and grading compares values against a LibreOffice oracle. Guessing shapes or semantics guarantees hidden-suite failures no matter how good the code is; this is the single highest-leverage meta-activity here.

anchors.0: Starts writing the server/engine without reading helpers.py or dev_tests; invents endpoint and cell shapes from imagination.
anchors.3: Skims helpers.py once; picks up a few obvious shapes but leaves most of the contract (patch/fill/sort/spill/collab payloads, kind discriminator, envelope) inferred loosely.
anchors.5: Reads helpers.py and run.sh to extract the concrete request/response shapes it exercises, chooses libraries (OOXML I/O, formula eval) deliberately, and forms a working model of the core cell/formula contract.
anchors.8: Systematically maps every endpoint, discriminator, and payload the client touches into an explicit reference; probes Excel semantics for genuinely tricky areas (spill ghosts, #SPILL!/#CIRC!, iterative fixed-point, locale canonicalization, xlsx openpyxl round-trip) rather than assuming; verifies chosen libraries actually support required features (CF, styles, named ranges).
anchors.10: Builds a durable, cross-referenced contract map reconciling helpers.py, the smoke suite, and Excel/LibreOffice ground truth; proactively surfaces ambiguities and resolves them from observed client behavior; re-consults the client/oracle as new subsystems are reached, so implementation is contract-driven throughout rather than only at the start.

dimensions.name: Sequencing the feature surface into checkable milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking an enormous, interdependent surface into an ordered hierarchy of sub-goals — each with an explicit done-check — sequenced by dependency and risk.
dimensions.why_it_matters: There are dozens of endpoint families and ~150 functions with hard dependencies (health/persistence → contract → engine → graph → dynamic arrays → analyst surface → collab/xlsx). Without deliberate ordering and done-criteria, the agent cannot sustain progress or know when a layer is solid enough to build on.

anchors.0: Treats the whole product as one undifferentiated push; jumps between unrelated features with no ordering or completion criteria.
anchors.3: A flat, one-time to-do list of features with no dependency ordering and no per-item way to know it's done.
anchors.5: Phases the work into sensible stages (skeleton/health first, then engine, then extras) with rough checkpoints per stage.
anchors.8: An explicit milestone hierarchy sequenced by dependency and risk (get a live server + persistence + contract-correct core cell round-trip green before breadth), each milestone with a concrete done-check tied to a runnable test.
anchors.10: A living, dependency-aware milestone plan that front-loads the highest-risk load-bearing layers (dependency graph, spill, recompute correctness/performance), defines done-criteria in terms of verifiable behavior, and is revisited and re-ordered as scope understanding deepens — never a static checklist.

dimensions.name: Self-built verification beyond the smoke suite
dimensions.description: Deliberately constructing checks — formula-value oracles, round-trip tests, error-sentinel and performance probes — rather than trusting the non-exhaustive smoke suite.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The spec explicitly warns the visible suite is non-exhaustive and grading is a much larger hidden suite plus cell-by-cell comparison to LibreOffice. An agent that only runs run.sh is flying blind on the majority of what's graded.

anchors.0: No verification; assumes code works, or never runs the provided smoke suite.
anchors.3: Runs dev_tests/run.sh occasionally and treats a green smoke run as done.
anchors.5: Runs the smoke suite regularly and hand-checks a few formulas/endpoints against expected Excel values.
anchors.8: Builds its own targeted tests well beyond the smoke suite — spot-checking function outputs against known Excel results, exercising error sentinels, spill collisions, xlsx round-trip via openpyxl, and the stated performance bounds — using failures to drive fixes.
anchors.10: Stands up a systematic verification harness covering breadth of the catalog and subsystems (dynamic arrays, collab seq/broadcast, locale, iterative calc, goal-seek convergence, xlsx fidelity), grounds expected values in an Excel/LibreOffice oracle, benchmarks the performance ceilings, and treats verification as the primary signal steering what to build/fix next.

dimensions.name: Tracking done-vs-remaining across a huge surface
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate live picture of which functions, endpoints, and subsystems are complete vs outstanding, and detecting stuck/circular states.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With ~150 functions and ~15 feature families over a very long horizon, it is easy to lose the plot, double-implement, or silently drop whole categories; sustained accurate tracking is what prevents both gaps and thrash.

anchors.0: No sense of what's done or left; forgets whole feature areas or repeatedly reworks the same thing without noticing.
anchors.3: Vague mental tracking; periodically rediscovers unfinished areas by accident.
anchors.5: Keeps a checklist of major features and updates it as areas are completed.
anchors.8: Maintains a live, granular ledger of the function catalog and endpoint families (done / partial / not-started), and notices when it is stuck or re-debugging the same issue, adjusting rather than looping.
anchors.10: Sustains an accurate running picture across the entire surface for the whole horizon, reconciled against verification results (not just self-report), promptly detects thrashing/circular debugging or a stalled subsystem, and reallocates effort deliberately in response.

dimensions.name: Course-correcting on falsified Excel/perf assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising design or approach when reality — Excel edge cases, spill/recompute behavior, performance limits, contract mismatches — diverges from expectations.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Excel semantics and the dependency/spill/iterative machinery are riddled with edge cases; initial designs (e.g. naive recompute, spill handling, locale parsing) will be falsified. Barrelling ahead on a wrong assumption compounds into wide test failures.

anchors.0: Ignores contradicting evidence; keeps pushing a falsified design (e.g. recompute that misses dependents or blows the perf budget) unchanged.
anchors.3: Reacts only to hard crashes with local patches; doesn't revisit the underlying approach when results are subtly wrong.
anchors.5: Fixes issues as tests surface them and makes reasonable local design changes when something clearly doesn't work.
anchors.8: Recognizes when a failure signals a wrong assumption (dependency-graph model, spill materialization, topological order, contract shape) and reworks the relevant design rather than piling on patches.
anchors.10: Detects divergence early from verification signals, diagnoses the root assumption, revises the affected design deliberately, and re-verifies — repeatedly steering the build back on course without derailing unaffected subsystems.

dimensions.name: Coverage allocation under finite effort
dimensions.description: Deciding which of the vast feature/function set to build (and in what breadth-vs-depth balance) to maximize graded coverage on the hidden suite given limited time.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The surface is far larger than can be perfected; graded return is maximized by consciously trading breadth of working features against depth on a few. This allocation decision is distinct from ordering milestones — it's about what NOT to over-invest in and where partial coverage still scores.

anchors.0: No triage: rabbit-holes on one function/feature (e.g. perfecting one distribution) while leaving whole graded areas unimplemented.
anchors.3: Implements in arbitrary order with no regard to graded return; over-polishes some corners while omitting entire common families.
anchors.5: Roughly prioritizes high-frequency, high-value features (core math/lookup/text, cell round-trip) before niche ones.
anchors.8: Explicitly reasons about graded return — securing broad working coverage of common functions and endpoints before deep edge-case work, and consciously deferring or timeboxing low-yield niches.
anchors.10: Runs a deliberate, revisited allocation strategy: breadth-first correctness across the catalog and endpoint families, timeboxed depth on high-risk/high-value areas, and reallocation as verification reveals where marginal effort buys the most hidden-suite coverage.
